adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and updates `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` to iterate over `event.destinationCalendar` and call `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` for each destination. `CalendarManager.createEvent` now calls the integration calendar service as `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`, and GoogleCalendarService was updated to select the matching destination calendar via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`. In contrast, `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` still derives `calendarId` from only the first array element (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;`) in create/update/delete paths. With multiple destination calendars (e.g., COLLECTIVE host calendars pushed into `evt.destinationCalendar` in handleNewBooking), Lark operations will always target the first destination calendar rather than the one matching the current credential/host, causing events for other hosts to be created/updated/deleted on the wrong calendar.
